svg.title: Financial database entity relationship diagram
svg.desc: Ten entity cards show selected actual columns and PostgreSQL data types from the finance schema. Company connects to filing. Filing and exact period connect to metric values, which are projected into income statement, balance sheet and cash flow views. Filing also connects to reports, sections and chunks. ID and REF indicate logical identifiers and join fields only, because all boxes are SQL views, not tables with enforced keys.
svg.text: finance schema · PostgreSQL views · selected columns shown
Logical identifier; multiple ID fields form one key
One row per filing + exact period + currency

g.text: CIK is issuer identity; ticker is a label
One row per accession; selected version
Instant or exact duration; no guessed quarter
One filing can have multiple reports
Exact duration; EPS is currency per share
Offsets address the exact cleaned report
Statement and metric rows use the filing's current processing scope.
Read the values with their status
Missing, conflicting, or review-required metrics are NULL, never invented zeroes.
Currency amounts keep base units. EPS keeps currency/share units.
Historical filings stay separate. A new default does not rewrite source evidence.
Underlying facts, report text, cells, and source provenance remain in sec.

svg.text: Logical read model: lines describe joins or projections between views, not enforced foreign keys. Not every view column is displayed.
